goal: Reduce the source's diagnostic maximum-rank summed NCCL kernel duration for the accumulated training step, retaining its step-time constraint and full correctness checks.
completion: One measured invocation is one complete DDP-accumulated GPT-2 training step on the seeded initial weights: optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True); forward+backward over the workload's accumulation_steps per-rank microbatches (input_ids=labels, shape (micro_batch, sequence_length)), each microbatch loss divided by accumulation_steps, with real NCCL gradient synchronization for the step (baseline: model.no_sync() on the first accumulation_steps-1 microbatches, the last microbatch's backward triggers the DDP all-reduce); then SGD optimizer.step() and torch.cuda.synchronize(). The completion boundary is after that synchronize: every rank's full gradients are bit-identical across ranks (atol=0.0, rtol=0.0 via rank-0 broadcast) and match, within workloads.json grad tolerances, the serial single-GPU reference that processes the identical global batch (all ranks' shards, each loss divided by the global microbatch count) from the same starting parameters; post-step parameters match the reference update within parameter tolerances; the accumulated loss is finite. Excluded from the repeated work: model/optimizer/input construction, initial-state reset, reference construction and checks, control barriers, profiling and report writing.
state_protocol: prepare(context, request): validates world_size equals request['workload']['world_size'], applies the source numerical policy (FP32, TF32 off, float32_matmul_precision 'highest', cudnn.benchmark off, threads, seeds), builds the GPT-2 LM head model with torch.manual_seed(20261020) on context['device'], wraps it in DDP (source baseline arguments), creates SGD (lr=0.001, momentum=0, weight_decay=0, foreach=False), generates per-rank synthetic microbatches from generator seeds 31000+rank (CPU copies of all ranks' shards kept for the rank-0 serial reference), snapshots the initial state_dict on CPU, and creates the source's separate gloo control group; no CUDA or model work happens at import time and no second process group default is initialized. reset(state): reloads the initial CPU state_dict, clears optimizer state, restores CPU/CUDA RNG snapshots, zeroes the run counter and the reference anchor; the source's zero_grad stays inside the timed run, and the process group is never destroyed. run(state): executes the full frozen step described in 'completion' and returns the accumulated (stacked sum of divided) loss; the framework times this call between CUDA synchronizations. observe(state, result): outside timing, clones loss/gradients/parameters to CPU, runs the source's relational checks and raises on violation: finite loss, exact cross-rank gradient equality via rank-0 broadcast on the default group, and on rank 0 the serial global-batch reference (reusing raw_model, restoring its full state_dict and gradients afterwards) with gradient/parameter tolerance comparisons and the +1-corruption negative control; for framework continuous step k>1 the serial reference is anchored to the observed post-step-(k-1) state_dict snapshot, i.e. the exact parameter point the distributed run started that step from. metrics(state, result, elapsed_ms): reports clean project metrics (step_ms, tokens_per_second from the unchanged work amount, tokens_per_step, effective_batch, parameter_count, workload dimensions, peak_allocated_bytes); the communication objective is collected by the framework's torch_communication collector in separately profiled invocations and is not fabricated here. models(state): {'gpt2': raw_model} for discovery and controlled replacement. set_mode/before_run: mode bookkeeping and the source's gloo control-group barrier outside the timer (safe to call repeatedly).
invariants: Workload dimensions and counts are read from request['workload'] (world_size, micro_batch, sequence_length, accumulation_steps) and the launched world size must equal workload world_size (gpt2_ddp_training.py:56-57); the workload row and its effective batch (world_size*micro_batch*accumulation_steps) are frozen by the request.

Per-rank input sharding is required workload semantics (request notes; make_inputs): each rank processes only its own microbatches, torch.randint(0, vocab_size, (micro_batch, sequence_length)) from generator seed 31000+rank; the serial reference consumes all ranks' shards in rank order.

Deterministic seeding for reference reproducibility: weights from torch.manual_seed(20261020) immediately before model construction; per-rank input generators 31000+rank (request notes; gpt2_ddp_training.py:24-32).

Numerical policy is frozen by the request/source: FP32 everywhere, torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False, cudnn.allow_tf32=False, float32_matmul_precision='highest', cudnn.benchmark=False, eager attention, all dropout 0, use_cache=False (common.py configure/make_model); the adapter must not change these policies.

Loss and gradient semantics (gpt2_ddp_training.py:36-45, request notes): each microbatch CE loss divided by accumulation_steps before backward, local divided losses summed per rank; the synchronized DDP gradients must equal the serial global-batch reference (each of the world_size*accumulation_steps microbatch losses divided by that global count) within grad_atol=1e-6, grad_rtol=1e-4.

The step's required work includes the gradient collectives themselves: real NCCL synchronization on the backend 'nccl' default process group with world_size 2 must happen inside the timed run() (request 'Required work includes the gradient collectives themselves').

Exact cross-rank gradient equality is asserted with atol=0.0, rtol=0.0 via rank-0 broadcast for every parameter (gpt2_ddp_training.py:81-86); implemented in observe() outside timing, raising on violation.

The timed step comprises zero_grad(set_to_none=True), all accumulation_steps forward/backward microbatches with the synchronization split, optimizer.step() and torch.cuda.synchronize() (gpt2_ddp_training.py:102-105; request measured-invocation definition); gradients must not be pre-cleared outside the timed region.

Post-step parameters must match the serial reference update within parameter_atol=1e-6, parameter_rtol=1e-4, with the source's SGD update rule lr=0.001, momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0 (gpt2_ddp_training.py:60, 88-91).
The +1-corruption negative control must be rejected by the gradient tolerance check (common.py negative_check); it is re-verified in observe().

Full required observations are preserved: accumulated loss, every parameter gradient and every updated parameter as detached CPU tensors, plus finite-loss and check outcomes; no performance counters or elapsed times in observations.

The communication objective is the framework-collected torch_communication.communication_kernel_sum_ms (per-rank sum of device NCCL kernel durations in separately profiled invocations, max across ranks, median over samples); the adapter's clean timing path (measure/profile modes) must stay free of extra collectives so the collector sees only the step's own communication.

Reset must restore the exact initial state before each measured step (gpt2_ddp_training.py:99-100) without destroying the process group, and repeated invocations from reset must reproduce the observations used as per-rank references.
assumptions: Baseline implementation choices reproduced from the source but not frozen requirements (request notes 'Baseline implementation choices, not frozen requirements'): DDP(bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True, broadcast_buffers=False), no_sync() on the first accumulation_steps-1 microbatches, foreach=False SGD, gloo control group for out-of-timing barriers; semantics-equivalent alternatives remain allowed under the quality checks and the step-time constraint.

The serial reference runs on rank 0 only, as in the source (gpt2_ddp_training.py:68-78), and reuses raw_model instead of allocating a second GPU model; the framework stores reference observations on CPU, so all observation tensors are CPU clones.

For framework multi-step control sequences (continuous steps without reset between), the source only ever checks its first accumulated step; this adapter generalizes that check by anchoring step k>1's serial reference to the observed post-step-(k-1) parameters so each step is compared from the same starting point without compounding tolerated first-step differences through the loss curvature.

The restore around the serial reference uses full state_dict snapshots because named_parameters() deduplicates GPT-2's tied lm_head/wte weight; restoring through a parameters-only snapshot would reload a stale tied key over the shared storage (this is what corrupted the previous revision's second continuous step).

The gloo control group timeout is raised from the source's 120s to 600s for hang tolerance while staying under the 900s worker timeout; barriers remain outside all timed regions, so measurement semantics are unchanged.

Model architecture constants (n_layer=12, n_embd=768, n_head=12, vocab_size=50257, n_positions=1024) are read at prepare() from the source workloads.json (request source_root) with the documented values as fallback; the SGD lr=0.001 is hardcoded in the source and kept as a constant.
Held-out workloads in workloads.json (longer_sequence) are not part of this frozen request; workload variants would supply different dimensions through request['workload'] using the same adapter.

GPU-side numerical divergence between NCCL-averaged gradients and the serial reference is governed by the source's grad/parameter tolerances, which observe() enforces exactly; no accuracy or convergence beyond reference fidelity is claimed.

Communication observations (communication_kernel_sum_ms) and the passive bucket inventory are collected by the framework's collector and diagnostics; the adapter installs no communication hook, and metrics() reports only clean project metrics rather than a fabricated objective value.

The worker has already bound CUDA and initialized the NCCL process group before prepare(); the adapter uses context['device'] for the model, inputs and all collectives and creates only the source's gloo control subgroup.
